label: Accounts sharing an identifier
description: Several accounts linked to one pseudonymous identifier — a device fingerprint, a phone-number hash, a UPI handle. Co-occurrence on an identifier is what turns a set of unrelated accounts into a candidate network.
confounders: A family sharing a handset, which is ordinary and extremely common.

A recycled phone number: telecoms reissue numbers, and two unrelated customers can hold the same number across time. This is why links are time-bounded and why a point-in-time query must respect the bounds.
A shared public terminal, a cyber cafe, or a branch tablet used to open several accounts legitimately.
Carrier-grade NAT, which puts thousands of unrelated subscribers behind one address.
notes: Shared identifiers are a real signal and a weak one, and the gap between those two facts is where this part of the interface earns its keep. The graph draws an inferred edge as a dashed line and a deterministic one as solid; the label says 'shares an identifier with', never 'is controlled by'. Expected band is MEDIUM rather than HIGH for exactly that reason: four accounts on one device is a reason to look, not a finding.
